title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
summary: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence in an array using DP or binary search.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body:
Given an integer array `nums`, return the **length** of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

The subsequence does not need to be contiguous, but elements must satisfy `nums[i] < nums[j]` for all `i < j` in the subsequence.

**Example:** `[8,2,4,3,6,12]` → `4` (the LIS is `[2,4,6,12]`)

sections.heading: Key Insight
sections.body:
**DP Approach (O(n²)):** For each position `i`, track the longest increasing subsequence ending at that index by extending any smaller element before it.

**Optimized (O(n log n)):** Use a `tails` array where `tails[k]` is the smallest tail element of all increasing subsequences of length `k+1`. Use binary search to update it. Note: the `tails` array is **not** the actual LIS, just a tool to compute its length.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.body:
**O(n²) DP Solution:**
- Create `dp` array where `dp[i]` = length of LIS ending at index `i`
- Initialize all `dp[i] = 1` (each element is a subsequence of length 1)
- For each `i`, check all previous indices `j < i`
- If `nums[i] > nums[j]`, update `dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1)`
- Return `max(dp)`

**O(n log n) Binary Search:**
- Maintain `tails` array where `tails[k]` = smallest tail of length-`(k+1)` subsequences
- For each number, binary search for its position in `tails`
- Replace or extend `tails` at that position
- Return length of `tails`

sections.heading: Complexity
sections.body:
**DP Approach:**
- Time: O(n²) - nested loops over array
- Space: O(n) - dp array

**Binary Search Approach:**
- Time: O(n log n) - n iterations × log n binary search
- Space: O(n) - tails array

approach: Initialize dp array with all 1s (base case: each element is LIS of length 1)
For each position i from 1 to n-1, iterate through all previous positions j
If nums[i] > nums[j], it can extend the subsequence ending at j
Update dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1) to track the longest extension
Return max(dp) as the overall longest increasing subsequence length
For O(n log n): maintain tails array and use bisect_left to find/update positions

complexity.time: O(n²) for DP approach, O(n log n) for binary search

quiz.q: What does dp[i] represent in the DP solution?
options: The length of the longest increasing subsequence in nums[0:i]
The length of the longest increasing subsequence ending at index i
The i-th element of the longest increasing subsequence
The number of increasing subsequences ending at index i
quiz.explain: dp[i] stores the length of the longest increasing subsequence that ends specifically at index i, not just within the first i elements.

quiz.q: In the O(n log n) approach, what does the tails array represent?
options: The smallest tail element for each possible LIS length
The indices of elements in the LIS
quiz.explain: tails[k] stores the smallest ending element among all increasing subsequences of length k+1. This is NOT the actual LIS, just a tool to efficiently compute its length using binary search.

quiz.q: Why do we use bisect_left instead of bisect_right in the optimized solution?
options: To find the leftmost position where num can replace a larger value
To maintain strict inequality (we want nums[i] < nums[j], not <=)
quiz.explain: bisect_left finds the leftmost position to insert/replace, ensuring we replace the first element >= num. This maintains strict increasing order and handles duplicates by replacing them rather than extending.
